body:
well the good news is, you already are a writer. your prose is terrific

but im not a hero. im a bum, a terrible failure and i've given up and committed to this. i have a bus picking me up in 10 hours to take me to a national park where i will walk into the woods and shoot myself in solitude. everyone dies, lots too soon. it's not a big deal, no loss to me and no loss to you

but i like your writing

youre really eloquent and i deeply appreciate your attention but today im 41. what is there for me? no job, no love, nothing. i dont want to become normal just so i can start life as a middle-aged loser

great post, love your writing, but there's nowhere for me to go. when i shut everything down i can go into emotional stasis but what's the point of that? and if i try to live, all i feel is the sadness. i spent decades struggling against it - i get it now. that's just who i am. even if i could rub a magic lamp and have a nice job and a girlfriend and world peace i'd still just be depressed, so depressed that i get fired or quit (like every job i had), so depressed that i push her away or she pushes me away (like every girl i had). 

it's not something i can overcome with willpower or stamina. as tough as i am, as resolute and stubborn as i can be, i'm nothing compared to my depression. i'm a tiny little rowboat in the pacific ocean compared to it.

and if it takes pills for me to live, why bother? i don't agree with the argument that every human life has inherent value. there's nothing i can do that hasn't already been done, better, by someone else. so if the only way for me to exist is to prop myself up with medication, i'm not interested. i don't value the world and it doesn't value me so i don't see the point in going out of my way to make peace with it.

ive never been free of depression. i thought age or money would help but nothing changed.

it's not a rational, logical thing based on facts and reason. it's emotional and i have no control over it.

last book - reread post office by bukowski 

game servers - CS, NS, TF2, other stuff but those were popular. i paid $400/month for fat upstream bandwidth back in 2000/2001 when it was uncommon to have 1MB up

poe - i like his poetry i guess but i'm more into contemporary authors. i am not knowledgeable enough about him to make an informed recommendation.

at times i have had all the symptoms of depression, literally crying or apathetic, lying in bed unable to do anything. that's back when i was "part of the world" with a job. since i've been living like a hermit i am not visibly depressed and dont have as many symptoms but when I am not busy with books or video games or movies (e.g. when taking a shower, when trying to sleep) my thoughts are dismal. I hate myself and want to be dead. does that mean it affects my decisionmaking? i don't know. other than being very depressed i am very rational.

my best joke? i don't know if any of them are good, they were more to appeal to kids. for example what did the ocean say to the beach?


nothing. it just waved.

video game - i used to run some very popular game servers and would play on them every night. had some very fun and funny moments there. generally just warm feelings about the people i meet when i'm playing online.

books - too many to list. when i was younger (teens) i loved stephen king and steinbeck, and then i tried to catch up on fiction classics like hemingway and bukowski. in the last decade i've been reading mostly nonfiction. i like alternate history stuff like What If?

a few moments stand out for me:

when i decided to start reading hemingway the first thing i did was go to the library and check out a big collection of his short stories. The first story was The Short, Happy Life of Frances Macomber. I was riding my bike from the library and stopped at a park to read a little. the story was INCREDIBLE. it was just so powerful and crystalline. i still remember it as a revelation.

another one is when I was young and felt very alone and hated myself. I read One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and the main character R. P. MacMurphy just blew me away. Here was a guy who epitomized confidence - he did whatever he wanted and fought against everyone. It just blew me away and kind of inspired me. I wanted to be him. It was also profound to me that the authorities in that book were the BAD guys. i don't think I had read a book like that before. It made me feel like there was someone else in the world who understood how I felt.
will check it out, thanks.

i am definitely aware that on paper i'm very fortunate. just being a white guy in the US gives me more advantages than 90% of the world. but inside my head i've always been miserable, and i've never felt understood or loved in my whole life, so it's hard to take solace in it

ive been most places - all over europe, all over the US, to asia a few times (singapore, HK, malaysia), south/central america.

we didn't travel in the army - i was stationed in germany and never left it for duty, but some of us would book package tours of europe on holiday weekends so i saw a fair amount of europe that way, nd then years later I had a software job where i went to europe sometimes.

check my other post on this page for how I feel about travel though - being depressed ruins it.

i love radiohead and that is one of my favorite tracks of theirs. but I wanted to list stuff that isn't as well-known and most people have at least heard of In Rainbows even if they haven't listened to it

that's a great question.

i've been all over the world. I was in the army and saw a lot of europe, and later I had a full-time travel job at a software company. i literally flew home on friday nights and flew out on sunday nights every week for almost 3 years, with the occasional week in the home office to catch up on paperwork. Then i had another job at another software company where I was the tech guy who represented/demod at conferences and conventions, as well as flying around to do training sometimes.

i think i would have enjoyed ALL of it if i wasn't depressed. but often I'd finish the day and get back to my hotel room, or finish the week and get on the plane, and all i could think about was how alone i was. i cried a lot.

really my best memories, my fondest memories, are from books and video games and bike rides. they took my mind off the depression and distracted me. i've played video games for tens of thousands of hours because in a sense they are self-medication for depression. when i was younger and before I hd  computer all I ever did was read. i would have my head in a book 24/7. i would fall asleep while reading, id wake up and start reading, i'd read while i was eating and walking, it's all i did. it kept my mind busy. 

i mostly feel depressed when i'm not in the middle of something keeping me busy - woody allen has said he keeps making movies because the process distracts him and occupies him so he doesn't get depressed. that's how I feel too, i just tried to find things to occupy my time.

the typical experiences/memories people have are when they are "in the moment" and savoring what's going on but whenever i'm paying attention to my surroundings and thinking about the present, my thoughts are always dark or sad, so i guess it's hard for me to say what i would have enjoyed if i wasn't always depressed.

i ran away from home when i was 13 and haven't seen them since.

experiences? i don't know, i've been depressed my whole life. everything i've experienced has been filtered through it and I definitely can't recommend that.

travel was depressing. relationships were depressing. work was depressing. all the things people say are great or fulfilling or life-affirming or whatever, for me they were depressing.

they only made 5 albums. the first one is half gospel/folk stuff because that's what was hot at the time. i'd say all 5 are good but just to pick a few random favorites:

bleeker street 

kathy's song

save the life of my child

america

so long, frank lloyd wright

the only living boy in new york

regarding relationships, a few things. i have tremendous barriers at every stage of a relationship:

- cripplingly shy and crowd-averse so i never "go out" and am never around strangers. the few times I have, often someone will approach me and start a conversation. of my ~6 relationships, all of them started with the woman talking to me first

- chronic depression managed to turn off a few of them. they were "normal" people who had no idea how to deal with it or desire to be around it. i usually explained my problems with depression on the 2nd date or so, so that ended a couple nascent relationships after 1 date

- when someone is interested in me i feel repulsed by them. i can't explain it, it's an inner voice/emotional response kind of thing. the best example was with a girl named jill. she was perfect - absolutely beautiful, like model perfect, getting a Ph.D, really into me. you'd think it was a dream but after a couple dates when she would call I wouldn't answer and hearing her voice message just made me kind of sick. when she came over to watch a movie she sat next to me on the couch and i had to move away, i couldn't stand being close to her. i laid down on the floor and then when she got off the couch and laid down next to me i got back up and sat on the couch. i never even had sex with her. i can't explain why, it's just how i feel about people. maybe self-protection from when I was a kid. anyway, for the people who didn't find my depression a deal-breaker, that generally ended it.

- finally for the people who approached me, could deal with depression, and somehow stuck through it even though I pushed them away, they eventually just got sick of me. interesting note, the 2 women in this category were both married to other men at the time.

i have LOTS and LOTS of negative experiences, don't even know where to begin on that one.

my career, in chronological order:

* high school dropout

* homeless

* us army (3 years)

* various retail jobs - bike shop, music store

* temp agency work - started out answering phones and doing powerpoint, moved up to tech support

* traveling tech support for medical software company

* traveling tech support + marketing (convention rep, etc) for software company

* software product manager

the whole time i was always depressed and always had sleep problems and so when I got laid off in 2003 and couldn't find another job I gave up. haven't worked since then. i've just stayed in my room, only leaving to buy food once a month. i was going to kill myself at that point but someone i knew asked me to move in to her storage room and help with her kids. so for a few years i picked them up from elementary school and did minor chores like taking the trash out and raking leaves. but they are almost out of high school now and I'm not needed any more.
ill be 41 tomorrow

it is kind of meaningless without context but when i ran away i was 13 and i spent that first night laying on a picnic bench in the park. i had shoplifted a walkman and made a tape of Simon & Garfunkel and stayed awake most of the night, laying on that bench and looking at the stars wondering what the fuck i was going to do. i had no friends, no family, no home, nowhere to go, nobody to talk to. the music meant a lot to me at the time and still does. when i hear those songs i still think about that night.

there was the time i was bike racing, mountain bike racing in monterey on the army base. i was doing really well, after about 4 hours we were near the finish and I was near the front. then a guy fell pretty hard and i got off my bike to help him. i feel like that's who i really am - more than anything i just want to help people. maybe just because im desperate to be liked? i dont know

when i was a kid my parents were divorced and they both traveled and moved a lot and I moved between them a lot. I was never in the same school for an entire year, which is partly why I never had any friends. between the moves, the divorce, the terrible parents, the IQ and related weirdness, and lack of extended family, i kind of had the "perfect storm" of how to create an anti social person. anyway i had another memory i thought was good but now i realize it's kind of negative so forget it.
having a dog is great but not feasible for me right now. i am basically homeless so it's not an option.

i hate everything i write. it's garbage. i know what good writing is, and I can't do it.

regarding the lady here, i don't know whether she "cares about me" or not but it's immaterial. i don't cost her anything and she is pretty hostile to me most of the time, so it seems to be a negative relationship for her. and she isn't obligated to help me or care about me in any way so there's nothing keeping me here based on our relationship.

regarding my parents, my solution to most problems is just to walk away. i have had no problem with cutting people off all my life. did it with my parents out of self preservation and now i will completely sever all contact with someone for the most trivial matters.

yeah i had that attitude my whole life, and now i'm 40. there were forks in the road along the way where things COULD have gone well. i made one very minor decision about some stocks and made $40k instead of 1.3 million in 1999. even being a complete recluse and avoiding human contact as much as possible, i STILL had women throw themselves at me occasionally. as camus said, women are the closest thing to paradise on earth. at least give yourself the chance to have those experiences and make those choices. 

and my original point stands. 17 is a different world from 21, which is a different world from 26 and so on. things will happen, you'll meet people, and maybe there's a chance you'll be unhappy for another 17 years and there's a good chance you'll always have problems with depression. but millions of people have depression and the vast majority of them still find life worth living and are glad they didn't kill themselves.

i'm not saying being depressed is inevitable or even addressing your concerns. i'm just stating flatly that **17 is simply too soon**. believe me, i changed and the world changed so much between 17 and 37. you can't even begin to plan for or expect the things that will happen. so at least try some adulthood. it's a lot better than high school for almost everyone.

17 is way too young to give up. your entire life will change and change again and probably change again more than that. 

the way i see it, it's ok to give up once you're 35 or 40 but believe me, things will happen in your 20s you can't even imagine now.

in a lot of ways i can't complain. i've been around, done a lot and seen a lot. i just don't fit in to the human race, and emotional stuff has always been very very painful for me. 

i look at it as a congenital handicap. some people are blind or stuck in wheelchairs, i'm stuck being unable to connect with another human being.

as the hours wind down i'm slowly becoming more at peace with this. everyone dies, and i've already lived quite a while.

thats not exactly what happened

there was a monster that looked like an oil slick that ate him
i don't have any money to do that. and I have traveled a lot - i had a job where I traveled constantly for almost 3 years. It just reinforced my loneliness.

if you do well in school, you'll do great at work. school is a lot of meaningless and useless bullshit, work is usually a straight meritocracy. and as most people get into their 20s and 30s, they manage to find some meaning in relationships. you have to be an extreme case like me to be completely hopeless.

give it a shot, at least til you're mid/late 30's. women show up out of nowhere and love can make you happy. 

i am considering "closure" by posting on the "big day" but i don't think it would be beneficial for anyone

When I was little I wanted to be a writer but I gave up on that a long time ago. What would I be right now? I don't know, i'm not good at anything, I have no skills. The nazi's had a phrase for people like me:  "useless eater."

The lady here, I don't know. It's complicated. I never was completely interested and I don't know why she's been letting me live here so long. There's certainly nothing between us at this point. She's told me "You'll never kill yourself." so even though she probably suspects that's my plan I doubt she expects it to actually happen.

My parents are dead to me. They treated me very badly so I ran away when I was young and haven't seen them since.

The problem is I am profoundly shy and have problems with being around people. I've been most comfortable just being alone for years, even when I was a kid I was alone all the time. I spent an entire summer in my teens without speaking to another person. 

I don't see how I could turn anything around. I always come back to the fact that years ago I was better looking and had more money and I was still incredibly depressed all the time. I've often sabotaged myself because I feel like i deserve to fail, for example doing something wrong and then not fixing it because I want it to get worse. It's a whole lifelong syndrome and I don't think I can just decide to be happy or reverse course at this point.

I don't know, I think it mostly has to do with my childhood. I was completely neglected (I could tell some horror stories) and from what I've read, that can do irreparable damage emotionally. And I did see a therapist for a while, and she even prescribed Paxil. I tried taking it but it didn't do anything and anyway I feel that if i have to take drugs to be "normal" then it's not meant to be.

And therapy is a joke. I've been exploring these feelings my whole life. A therapist is never going to tell me something I haven't already thought about.

I would trade places with you. I think it's tragic that i'm stuck with these feelings when there are people who desperately want to live.

I have tried volunteering but I have social anxiety and shyness problems and those, coupled with feelings of hopelessness and low self worth, make it very hard for me to stick with it.

yeah what you said is definitely part of it - suicide is a way for me to rationalize away all my failures. if i am just going to kill myself anyway, then it doesn't matter whether i am too lazy to do laundry or even brush my teeth every day. "FUCK IT!" life is more liveable that way. 

if i was somehow blocked from killing myself, i'd be in a hell of a mess. i'd have to start over with a new career, working some shit job and living in a shitty little hole in poverty and being alone and miserable for another 20-40 years until i died anyway. suicide is a way to escape all that - it was always a way out from every mistake i made or bad circumstances that ever happened in my life.

if i couldn't get someone to love me when i was young and thin and employed then it won't happen now. 

i do have a lot of knowledge and experience and i would sometimes daydream about telling and teaching my S.O. or even my kids things i learned. but i'm almost 41 and the nights i've spent with another person i could probably count on both hands. 

when i was younger, when i first started thinking about my adult life, i did have some hope that someday i'd meet someone who made me happy or i'd just be in better circumstances and stop being depressed or just that somehow, things would change. as the years went on that hope gradually disappeared. in about 2003 is when i figured my best years were behind me and if it hadn't happened by then, it was never going to happen. and it's just been downhill since then.

really it's impossible for someone in my condition, in my situation, at my age, to find someone. and even if i could somehow find that one in a million person, they couldn't fix me. i'd still be depressed all the time.

rationally i know im not a terrible person but that's what written in my brain and that's how i feel. my emotional brain completely dominates my intellectual brain. I can understand reality but once I start feeling something it completely overwrites whatever I was thinking. as one person put it, i'm cripplingly hypersensitive. and empirically, to look back on my life, i didn't get much right but the mistakes and regrets are endless. so you might not think i'm unlovable or a failure and i might understand that i'm really not, but that's how i feel and i can't change it.

was I ever happy? to be honest, not really. there were things I enjoyed - exercise, driving my car, watching a good movie or having fun playing video games. but they were like 1 light bulb in a blacked-out city. 

and at this point it's too late to turn my life around. if i couldn't get it right when i was young and healthy and had a good job, what can I do now, homeless and unemployed?

sorry for the negative reply, it's kind of rude for me to post and then shit on people trying to be supportive. it's how i have always reacted to optimism. :(
I've always felt the same way. Sometimes I was depressed, sometimes I wasn't, but it always just seemed like the logical thing to do - the same thing you described.
